---
title: "Requests, Execution, and Result Ownership"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING concept

This page explains the current candidate design. It does not define request
signatures, receipt contents, workspace validation, or failure behavior; the
linked Runtime Contract remains the sole authority.
:::

## Design pressure

Notebook analysis must remain understandable after a kernel restart, when two
different questions share a model, and when evidence is revisited later.
Hidden mutable state such as a current view, latest result, or implicit solve
would make those situations ambiguous.

## Selected abstraction {#run-request-result-ownership}

`CircuitRun` owns the sealed Plan's runtime context, workspace, requests,
receipts, and terminal execution. A Ref and Spec describe one exact question;
`solve()`, `evaluate()`, and `optimize()` perform different kinds of real
work and return typed Results. A Result owns one verified answer and its exact
evidence identity, while `resolve()` retrieves that answer without making a
new computation.

`explain()` occupies the useful middle ground: it returns a typed
`ExplanationResult` that makes the bound request reviewable without starting
an execution job, numerical analysis, or workspace write.

## Problem solved

The model can support a response surface, a physical quantity, and an
optimization independently without one request changing the meaning of
another. Exact receipt-backed identity also lets a consumer reconstruct and
resolve a request across processes instead of depending on in-memory caches or
a Notebook's execution order.

## Intentionally not owned

This concept does not let a Run mutate circuit physics, make a result the
Run's current state, or select a latest request implicitly. It does not make
presentation an execution action, and it does not turn a receipt into a new
physical or product authority.
